clue.text: IT interface is something very difficult to put back

indicators.note: putting a word back sends its letters the other way, last to first

blocks.note: the 's contraction of is
a pig of a job is something very hard to do
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: A grumble that some computer connection is a nightmare to refit.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the little word 'to' is turned round; S and PIG stand as they are. A pig is informal for a horribly awkward task.
explanation.definitionFit: A spigot is the plug end of a pipe that slots into a socket, so it is a connecting point; the setter extends that to computing.

clue.text: Perhaps tête-à-tête is nothing at all about nothing

zero, the round figure for nothing

explanation.surface: Someone claims an intimate chat amounts to nothing much at all.
explanation.walkthrough: A tête-à-tête is also an S-shaped two-seater couch, which is why 'Perhaps' flags it as one example. Sweet FA (Fanny Adams) is British slang for nothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A tête-à-tête is a kind of settee for two facing sitters, an example of the broader piece of furniture.

clue.text: Outside ruin in Delphi spending day raving about loving Greece

explanation.surface: Someone in ancient ruins at Delphi, raving about a love of Greece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delphi' makes the surface feel Greek, but it is only fodder; 'ruin' is the word that sits in the middle, and 'about' is a one-letter abbreviation joining the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: A philhellene is an admirer of Greece; the adjective describes fondness for Greek people and culture.
